title: Judas Iscariot
lead: One of the Twelve, who handed Jesus over to the chief priests. The Gospels say he kept the group's money, was paid for the handing over, and died soon after. Why he did it, and how his choice relates to God's plan and Scripture's predictions, has been debated ever since.

sections.b: All four Gospels list Judas among the Twelve and say he handed Jesus over (Mark 3:19; 14:10–11, 43–45). Matthew adds the thirty pieces of silver and his death by hanging (Matthew 26:14–16; 27:3–10); Acts tells a different account of his death in a field (Acts 1:16–20). Luke and John say Satan entered him (Luke 22:3; John 13:27). John calls him a thief (John 12:6) and "the son of ruin" (John 17:12). Proposed meanings of "Iscariot" include "man of Kerioth," a town in Judea, or a word related to the dagger-men (sicarii), but no explanation is certain.
